questions.question: When you see a green arrow on a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow. First, yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow. First, yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane to make the turn. Always yield to vehicles and pedestrians who are already in the intersection.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road angles toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is coming up.
You are approaching a construction area.
You must turn left soon.
The road will become narrower.

questions.explanation: A solid line marks the edge of the road. When it angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: When you see a yellow arrow on a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Do not park on the right side of the street.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is the minimum time someone must spend in jail for a first DUI conviction?

options.text: Three days
10 days
20 hours
96 hours

questions.explanation: A DUI conviction requires a minimum of three days in jail. Additional fines and fees will also apply.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: When passing traffic moving in the same direction.
During the day only.
Anytime.
When you are turning.

questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid yellow lines cannot. The only exception is when you are making a turn.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs tell you?

options.text: School zones ahead.
No passing zone.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have words on it to confirm this.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Always check mirrors and use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: Your car is faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pass the bicycle.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing bicycles. A cyclist might have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object in the road. Always drive carefully around cyclists.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn them to the right.
Turn them to the left.
Keep them straight.
Leave the transmission in neutral.

questions.explanation: When parked downhill, turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Alaska requires each registered vehicle to have:

options.text: One license plate on the back.
Two license plates: one on the front and one on the back.
No specific number of license plates.
One license plate on the front.

questions.correctAnswerText: One license plate on the back.
questions.explanation: You must have one license plate on the rear of your vehicle with month and year tabs visible. A white light should shine on the rear plate so the numbers can be seen from at least 50 feet away.

questions.question: A speed restriction sign:

options.text: Can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
Has a triangular shape.
Is blue with black letters.
Shows the recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows the recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Curve and turn warning signs often show a recommended speed for that area. You may drive faster in good weather, but you should slow down in rain, snow, or icy conditions.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a DUI, your license will be revoked for at least:

options.text: 30 days.
60 days.
Six months.
90 days.

questions.explanation: If you refuse a breath test or your blood alcohol level is 0.08 percent or higher, your license will be revoked for a minimum of 90 days.

questions.question: A reckless driving conviction will result in:

options.text: A $50 fine and four points on your driving record.
A warning for the first time and a $50 fine for the second time.
Suspension of your driving privileges.
Revocation of your driving privileges.

questions.explanation: Reckless driving means ignoring the safety of people and property. A conviction will result in your license being revoked.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true?

options.text: Driving at high speeds wears out tires.
Driving at the same speed for too long can cause drowsiness.
Driving at high speeds uses more gasoline.
You cannot drive below the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot drive below the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: High speeds cause tire wear and poor fuel economy. Change your speed sometimes to stay alert. You do not have to drive at the maximum speed limit, but do not drive so slowly that you block traffic.

questions.question: A driver who fails to restrain passengers under age 16 may be fined up to ____ per passenger.
questions.explanation: You can be fined up to $50 for each passenger under 16 who is not properly restrained. You may also get two demerit points.

questions.question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines are doubled in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you to hazards ahead and are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of an area with low clearance.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking this rule can result in a penalty.
